lines.text: In 1964, a newspaper reported that thirty-eight people watched a woman being attacked in New York. And not one of them helped.
lines.say: In nineteen sixty-four, a newspaper reported that thirty-eight people watched a woman being attacked in New York... And not one of them helped.
lines.say11: [serious] In 1964, a newspaper reported that thirty-eight people watched a woman being attacked in New York. [pause] And not one of them helped.

lines.text: Her name was Kitty Genovese. The story shocked the country.
lines.say11: [softly] Her name was Kitty Genovese. The story shocked the country.

lines.text: Psychologists built a whole theory on it. The bystander effect. The more people watch, the less anyone helps.
In a famous lab test, people heard someone having a seizure. Alone, eighty-five percent ran to help. In a group of five, only thirty-one percent did.
But the thirty-eight witnesses? That number didn't hold up.
lines.say: But... the thirty-eight witnesses? That number didn't hold up.
lines.say11: [dramatic pause] But... the thirty-eight witnesses? [beat] That number didn't hold up.

lines.text: Most neighbors only heard noises, late at night. Very few actually saw anything.
At least one person called the police. And a neighbor, Sophia Farrar, ran outside and held Kitty in her arms.
lines.say11: At least one person called the police. [softly] And a neighbor, Sophia Farrar, ran outside... and held Kitty in her arms.

lines.text: Decades later, the newspaper itself admitted the story was badly exaggerated.
So is the bystander effect fake? Not quite. In the lab, it's real.
lines.say: So is the bystander effect fake? ... Not quite. In the lab, it's real.
lines.say11: [thoughtful] So is the bystander effect fake? [short pause] Not quite. In the lab, it's real.

lines.text: But in 2019, researchers studied real security camera footage of more than two hundred public fights in three countries.
lines.say: But in twenty nineteen, researchers studied real security camera footage of more than two hundred public fights in three countries.

lines.text: In nine out of ten, at least one stranger stepped in. And the more people were around, the more likely someone helped.
lines.say11: [surprised] In nine out of ten, at least one stranger stepped in. And the more people were around... the more likely someone helped.

lines.text: So the lesson flips. Crowds aren't cold. The danger is the first few seconds, when everyone waits for someone else to move.
So be the first one. Others will follow.
lines.say11: [warm] So be the first one. [pause] Others will follow.

lines.text: Next file: the experiment that made obedience look easy. Some of the people in it didn't believe it was real.
lines.say11: [mysterious] Next file: the experiment that made obedience look easy. [whispers] Some of the people in it didn't believe it was real.
